text:
alex: Quick sketch — propose a small 'demux adapter' layer between prefix cache and slab allocator to handle multi-tenant eviction policies without leaking slab internals.
mina: short version: adapter holds tenant affinity + soft-lease bookkeeping, returns handles instead of direct residency pointers.
sam: why not just extend current lease API? feels similar.
alex: main difference: adapter normalizes responses for different backends (local slab vs shared slab vs remote warmup). decouples eviction decisions from caller correctness needs.
ria: example flow pls? :thinking_face:
alex: root msg:

```
client -> prefix-cache -> demux-adapter -> slab-manager
                                          -> prefetcher
```
adapter provides `AcquireHandle(prefix, consistency_hint)` which may return:
- handle(state="resident", slot=...) OR
- handle(state="stale_readback", fetch_token=...) OR
- handle(state="pending_prefill", ticket=...)

alex: callers only use handle.Read() / handle.Release(). adapter guarantees read-after-write for callers that asked `consistency_hint=strong` by blocking or routing to fallback model.

sam: so adapter needs to know tenant QoS and hotkey priority to pick eviction victim? that's a lot of logic.

alex: yes but centralizing it avoids duplicating heuristics across codepaths. also can expose simple signals: `should_pin`, `evictable_score`.

mina: correctness: how do we prevent ABA-style races if adapter migrates slot ownership during an in-flight read?

jeff: we should keep a short-lived pin mechanism: AcquireHandle pins slot with a generation tag; Release decrements pin. Migration requires waiting for pin==0 OR performing a copy-on-write handoff while new readers are diverted to the copied slot.

ria: copy-on-write handoff for hot prefixes might be expensive.

sam: tradeoff: either block new reads (increase latency) or allow stale reads (weaker consistency) or pay copy cost. we should pick defaults per route.

alex: exactly — adapter has policies per-route: {latency_sensitive: prefer stale_reads}, {consistency_sensitive: block or fallback}, {cost_sensitive: copy-on-write rare}.

mina: can we reuse existing metrics? need metrics to know when adapter routes to fallback vs stale vs COW.

alex: propose these metrics: `adapter.route.count` by outcome, `adapter.eviction.delay_ms`, `adapter.copy_cost_bytes`, `adapter.pin_conflicts`.

jeff: rollout plan? feature flag gated.

alex: plan:
1) implement adapter shim with no-op policy that mimics old behavior (safety net)
2) add per-route policy config + metrics
3) enable heuristics in canary (low-traffic cluster)
4) run chaos test where we force migrations and measure pin conflicts + tail latency

sam: tests: unit tests for generation tags, integration smoke where we simulate handoff while read ongoing, and e2e with tenant fairness load.

ria: ops-bot, can you add a ping to infra to bump test infra GPU mem so we can simulate large slabs?
ops-bot: @infra-team FYI: request to provision larger mem nodes for kv-cache e2e sim (details in #eng-runtime). Ticket: IRON-701

mina: one more corner: what about metrics for fairness eviction—need per-tenant eviction counts and reclaimed bytes.
alex: add `adapter.evictions.by_tenant` and `adapter.reclaimed_bytes.by_tenant`.

mina: ok, I'm +1 to the adapter concept. I'll draft a short RFC with API sketches and tests.

sam: curious: will this help prefix prefill jitter where prefill storms thrash slab? could add admission.
alex: yes adapter can also act as admission gate for prefill; admit based on global budget and tenant windows.

ria: sounds promising. please drop the RFC link here when ready.
alex: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
